subject: BlueForge adapter: proposed API v3 deprecation & mitigation request
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@blueforge.io>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Upcoming API v3 - impact on BlueForge adapter

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from our engineering lead: we just started a compatibility sweep against your announced API v3 changes and several breaking points will require non-trivial rewrites in our adapter (auth header shape, streaming framing changes, and the new tokenization param). We understand product teams need to iterate, but BlueForge ships a connector integrated into three customer-managed deployments.

Can you share: 1) firm deprecation timeline for the current v2 endpoints, 2) whether Redwood will publish a compatibility shim or compatibility flags, and 3) whether partners can access a mirrored staging endpoint to validate migrations before cutover?

We've attached our initial migration plan and a short list of high-priority customers who will need longer lead time. This is material to our roadmap and we wanted to raise it early.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call.

—Alex
Alex Carter
Head of Integrations, BlueForge Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@blueforge.io>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-11T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming API v3 - impact on BlueForge adapter

Alex — thanks for surfacing this and for the migration plan. Looping in Vanessa (partner engineering) and Marcus (SDK/runtime) so we can triage specific compatibility gaps.

Initial response: we haven't finalized hard deprecation dates internally but v3 is target for Q3 ship; we expect an announced deprecation window aligned to release. That said, we recognize ISV adapters like BlueForge need predictability. Vanessa / Marcus — can you take a look at the attachment and propose options for: compatibility flags, a shim package, and partner staging access?

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Partner Programs, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alex Carter <alex.carter@blueforge.io>
Date: 2028-03-14T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming API v3 - impact on BlueForge adapter

Hi all — quick technical options after a spike on the reported items. I reviewed BlueForge's migration doc and sketched a compatibility matrix (attached). High-level options: 

1) Compatibility flags on the v3 runtime: allow v2-style auth framing + legacy streaming framing behind a flag. Pros: minimal infra. Cons: ongoing maintenance and could increase tech debt.

2) Publish an official SDK shim package (redwood-adapter-compat) that rewrites v2 calls to v3 shapes at the client side. Pros: isolates partner changes, short runway. Cons: doesn't cover managed customer deployments that embed raw calls.

3) Dual-endpoint: run v2 compatibility proxy for partners enrolled in the partner program for 6 months after v3 GA; we can route partner tokens to the proxy. Pros: best for partners with limited engineering bandwidth. Cons: requires reserved infra and SLA commitments.

For validation we can: a) provide a nightly mirror endpoint (staging.redwood.partners/blueforge) with a stable test vector suite, and b) ship a small test harness (pytest-based) that runs their adapter against our mirror. I can own the harness and the compat-matrix.xlsx.

Questions for partner: what minimal window do you need (months)? Which customers are in-scope for mirror access? Also, BlueForge — do you prefer a shim package or a proxy?

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Runtime Integrations
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@blueforge.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@edgeconsult.com>
Date: 2028-03-18T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming API v3 - impact on BlueForge adapter

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the options and the offer to own the harness. From BlueForge's perspective: 

- We need a minimum of 9 months of compatibility for our largest pilots (two healthcare customers running on-prem). Those customers require a maintenance SLA for the bridge period — critical bug fixes must be prioritized.
- Prefer a proxy/dual-endpoint approach for those managed customers. For other customers a shim SDK would be fine.
- We will need a mirrored staging endpoint and your test vectors to be feature-complete at least 8 weeks prior to our planned config freeze (we have an internal freeze on 2028-08-01).

If Redwood can commit to a proxy for enrolled partners + nightly mirror + the harness and a prioritization queue for critical fixes during the compatibility window, we can accept a shorter public deprecation (6 months) but ask that you guarantee partner proxy availability for 9 months.

Attaching BlueForge_migration_plan_v1.pdf with customer-impact notes. Happy to set up a partner sync next week.

—Alex
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@blueforge.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Upcoming API v3 - impact on BlueForge adapter

Alex — thanks, and thanks for the detail. We ran this up the product and infra leads. Proposal (compromise) below: 

- Public deprecation for v2: 6 months after v3 GA. We will publish exact GA + deprecation dates with v3 release notes.
- Partner compatibility guardrail: Redwood will provide a partner-only compatibility proxy for enrolled partners for 9 months after v3 GA (meets your ask). The proxy is scoped to request/response shape translation and legacy streaming framing.
- Test/validation: we will provide a nightly mirror staging endpoint and the pytest harness (owned by Marcus). We will publish a partner test vector suite and onboarding checklist 10 weeks before GA.
- SLA & bug prioritization: during the 9-month proxy window, critical compatibility regressions reported by enrolled partners will be triaged within 48 hours and scheduled into the next partner patch release. Non-critical regressions follow normal cadence.
- Enrollment: we'll require a short MOU for partners wanting proxy access (light legal + capacity commitment). I've attached a draft MOU (redwood-partner-mou-draft.docx).

Next steps: if BlueForge agrees to the MOU scope and the 9-month proxy commitment, we'll schedule a technical onboarding (Marcus + infra) and lock the test-vector dates. Marissa will coordinate the MOU and partner program enrollment.

Alex — can you confirm acceptance or list exceptions by EOD next Wednesday so we can loop infra capacity planning in?

Thanks — Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Partner Engineering, Redwood Inference
